$comment: Image CVE exceptions (ADR-0015 item 4). Each entry: id, image (postgres|keycloak|redis|caddy|otelcollector, or the release images api|bff|migrator, #119), package, justification (20+ chars), issue (#n), added and expires (YYYY-MM-DD, expires at most 90 days after added). Matching is exact. A component on the request path of a LAN-reachable service (Caddy, Keycloak and its Java libraries, the BFF, the Api) needs Marco's recorded approval, a reachability argument and an expiry of at most 30 days; Caddy has no exception without it (#120, G3 S-120-07). See docs/runbooks/ci-security-gates.md.

CVE-2026-78659 (GO-2026-6603), Go standard library go1.26.8 in the Caddy binary, fixed in Go 1.26.9. Nature: HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion via Trailer headers (High). No Caddy release contains Go 1.26.9 or later or golang.org/x/net 0.60.0 or later as of 2026-10-17 (v2.11.7 is the latest release; the pinned digest sha256:d8542f48d34a is unchanged). Reachable once deployed: Caddy is the LAN edge and parses this input before any authentication; the stack is not deployed today (#132, #29), so the risk rests on time and on the deploy guard, and this entry is void once Caddy runs anywhere reachable. Time-boxed under ADR-0015 item 4 (#142), 14 days, expires 2026-10-31; `stackctl up` refuses while this entry is present, expired or not, until the Caddy bump removes it. Exception approved by Marco 2026-10-17 under #142.

CVE-2026-92392 (GHSA-7jvw-75gf-2h34), curl 8.22.0-r0 (Alpine apk) in the Caddy image: HTTP/2 upload use-after-free (High, AV:N/AC:H). Fix state at scan time: unknown, Alpine has no fixed package yet; upstream fixed it in curl 8.23.0. The advisory affects both the curl tool and libcurl. Class (a), not loaded, not executed. Caddy is a static Go binary (CGO_ENABLED=0) that uses Go's net/http, so it loads no libcurl. The only package in the image that depends on libcurl is curl (apk info -r libcurl on the new digest, run with --network none, 2026-10-22; the only files linking libcurl.so are /usr/bin/curl and /usr/lib/libcurl.so.4.8.0). Nothing runs curl: the healthcheck is `nc -z` (busybox), the overlay sets no entrypoint, the --network none sh one-shots ban curl by test, the smoke test uses busybox wget, and `caddy adapt` does not call it. The flaw needs an outbound HTTP/2 upload to a malicious server, which no process in the image makes; there is no shell route from the network. libcurl in this image rests on the same argument and is not reported separately by the scan. Caddy is the LAN edge, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: approved by Marco 2026-10-22; added 2026-10-22, expires 2026-11-21, 30 days. Ends when Alpine ships curl 8.23.0 and the caddy tag is rebuilt; bump the digest then; not renewed.
